addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

FROM node:18-bookworm

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    git \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /app

# Clone the repository, pin to the base commit, then strip .git so the agent
# cannot inspect the fix PR or future history (anti-cheat). Re-init a single
# base commit tagged harbor_base so the verifier can reset test files and
# git apply still works without upstream history.
RUN git clone https://github.com/IvarK/AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode /app \
 && git -C /app checkout 5b8d4296e697f3ea83a9fea5aa84eb5e4f8d4385 \
 && rm -rf /app/.git \
 && git -C /app init -q \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h add -A \
 && git -C /app -c user.email=h@l -c user.name=h commit -q -m base \
 && git -C /app tag harbor_base

# Pre-install the repo's dependencies so verify time does not wait on the network.
RUN npm install --prefix /app

# Visual evidence readable by the agent at /app/.harbor_assets/.
# tests/ and solution/ are intentionally NOT copied into the image —
# the harness supplies them at verify time.
RUN mkdir -p /logs /app/.harbor_assets
COPY assets/ /app/.harbor_assets/

CMD ["bash"]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Behavioral verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-2843-mm.
3	# Applies the synthetic test patch (vitest unit test for notation formatting),
4	# installs test-only deps, runs f2p tests into a JUnit XML report, and calls verifier.py.
5	# NEVER greps candidate source for the fix — the test runs the production code.
6	set -uo pipefail
7	mkdir -p /logs/verifier
8	STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
9	STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
10	REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml
11	
12	: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"
13	
14	ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
15	trap ensure_reward EXIT
16	
17	cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
18	
19	# ------------------------------------------------------------------
20	# Reset EVERY path the patch touches to harbor_base (idempotency +
21	# agent-edit protection). For new files not in harbor_base, the
22	# checkout fails silently and rm -f removes any leftover from a
23	# previous run.
24	# ------------------------------------------------------------------
25	_patch_paths=$(
26	  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
27	    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
28	  } | sort -u )
29	for _p in $_patch_paths; do
30	  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
31	done
32	git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u) 2>/dev/null || true
33	
34	echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
35	git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
36	  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
37	  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
38	  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
39	
40	echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
41	# Install vitest and jsdom without modifying package.json/package-lock.json.
42	# jsdom is the virtual browser environment required by vitest for this test.
43	npm install --no-save --no-package-lock --legacy-peer-deps \
44	    vitest@1.6.0 jsdom@24.1.3 \
45	    >> "$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
46	  || { echo "ERROR: npm install failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }
47	
48	echo "== running f2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
49	# Run the notation test suite and emit a JUnit XML report.
50	# vitest exits non-zero when tests fail; we capture the exit code and continue to parse the report.
51	npx vitest run \
52	    --config /app/vitest.config.mjs \
53	    --reporter=junit \
54	    --outputFile="$REPORT" \
55	    /app/javascripts/__tests__/notation.test.js \
56	    >> "$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
57	  || echo "(vitest exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
58	
59	echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
60	# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
61	# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
62	# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
63	RUBRIC=""
64	if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
65	  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
66	             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
67	  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
68	fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-2843-mm.
# Applies the synthetic test patch (vitest unit test for notation formatting),
# installs test-only deps, runs f2p tests into a JUnit XML report, and calls verifier.py.
# NEVER greps candidate source for the fix — the test runs the production code.
set -uo pipefail
mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
REPORT=/logs/verifier/report.xml

: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reset EVERY path the patch touches to harbor_base (idempotency +
# agent-edit protection). For new files not in harbor_base, the
# checkout fails silently and rm -f removes any leftover from a
# previous run.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
_patch_paths=$(
  { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
    sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
  } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -f "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
git -C /app clean -fdq -- $(printf '%s\n' $_patch_paths | xargs -r -n1 dirname | sort -u) 2>/dev/null || true

echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== installing pinned test-only deps ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Install vitest and jsdom without modifying package.json/package-lock.json.
# jsdom is the virtual browser environment required by vitest for this test.
npm install --no-save --no-package-lock --legacy-peer-deps \
    vitest@1.6.0 jsdom@24.1.3 \
    >> "$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: npm install failed" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

echo "== running f2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Run the notation test suite and emit a JUnit XML report.
# vitest exits non-zero when tests fail; we capture the exit code and continue to parse the report.
npx vitest run \
    --config /app/vitest.config.mjs \
    --reporter=junit \
    --outputFile="$REPORT" \
    /app/javascripts/__tests__/notation.test.js \
    >> "$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(vitest exited non-zero; parsing report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge - SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing. The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Verifier for IvarK__AntimatterDimensionsSourceCode-2843-mm.

Parses the vitest JUnit XML report written by test.sh and computes a reward:
  1.0  — every f2p test passes AND every p2p test passes
  0.0  — anything else (a strict subset of f2p passing, or f2p all pass but a p2p regressed)

Reward policy is binary: partial f2p progress is not scored, since the four count keys
(f2p_passed/f2p_total/p2p_passed/p2p_total) already carry how close a submission got.
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

CONF   = json.load(open('/tests/config.json'))
F2P    = CONF['f2p']
P2P    = CONF['p2p']
REPORT = '/logs/verifier/report.xml'
REWARD = '/logs/verifier/reward.txt'

_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            json.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=sys.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


def load_results():
    """Return {test_identifier: 'pass'|'fail'|'skip'} from the JUnit XML."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(REPORT):
        return results
    try:
        tree = ET.parse(REPORT)
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in tree.iter('testcase'):
        # JUnit name includes the describe block: "Suite > test name"
        name = f"{tc.get('classname', '')}::{tc.get('name', '')}".strip(':')
        failed  = any(c.tag in ('failure', 'error') for c in tc)
        skipped = any(c.tag == 'skipped' for c in tc)
        results[name] = 'skip' if skipped else ('fail' if failed else 'pass')
    return results


def matched(idents, results):
    """Match each configured identifier against reported names (substring/regex tolerant)."""
    out = {}
    for ident in idents:
        hit = next(
            (v for k, v in results.items() if ident in k or re.search(re.escape(ident), k)),
            None
        )
        out[ident] = hit or 'missing'
    return out


def main():
    r = load_results()

    f2p_matched = matched(F2P, r)
    p2p_matched = matched(P2P, r)

    f2p_passing = [k for k, v in f2p_matched.items() if v == 'pass']
    p2p_passing = [k for k, v in p2p_matched.items() if v == 'pass']

    reward = canon_reward(
        len(f2p_passing), len(F2P),
        len(p2p_passing), len(P2P),
        rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]),
    )

    # Per-test outcomes, flat f2p::<name>/p2p::<name> = 1.0/0.0. Without these,
    # a gate run (e.g. nop) can only see the aggregate pass count, so an f2p
    # test that is inert (passes with no fix at all) is invisible to it.
    for ident, verdict in f2p_matched.items():
        _canon[f"f2p::{ident}"] = 1.0 if verdict == 'pass' else 0.0
    for ident, verdict in p2p_matched.items():
        _canon[f"p2p::{ident}"] = 1.0 if verdict == 'pass' else 0.0

    print(json.dumps({
        'reward': reward,
        'f2p': f2p_matched,
        'p2p': p2p_matched,
        'all_results': r,
    }))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

Yes, the standard `node:18-bookworm` image (based on Debian bookworm) does include Python 3 by default, along with other build tools.

According to a detailed analysis of Node.js Docker images, when testing the newer `node:22` image (also Debian bookworm-based), running `docker run --entrypoint bash node:22 -c 'python3 --version'` successfully returns a Python version, confirming Python 3 is present.

The same source notes this isn't an isolated inclusion — Python is not the only "unexpected" package in this image, as it also includes the entire GNU Compiler Collection. This happens because the official Node.js Docker images are built on top of Debian's `buildpack-deps` image, which bundles common build tools and interpreters (including Python, GCC, etc.) to support compiling native Node.js addons.

As a result, these full (non-slim, non-alpine) bookworm-based Node images tend to be quite large — the node:22 image has a grand total of 661 packages in it, contributing to an image size of over 1GB.

So for `node:18-bookworm` specifically (same Debian bookworm base as `node:22` in the tests above), you can expect `python3` to be available out of the box. If you want a minimal image without Python/GCC/etc., you'd want to use `node:18-bookworm-slim`, `node:18-alpine`, or a distroless Node image instead.
